title: Farmers blockade the port of Zeebrugge
location: Zeebrugge port and surrounding access roads, West Flanders
organizer: Algemeen Boerensyndicaat (ABS) called members to join; exact organizer of the port blockade needs confirmation
participants_original: The Guardian reports 400 farmers had started a week of protests near Antwerp; it does not say that 400 were simultaneously at the Zeebrugge port blockade.
threshold_50_evidence: S001 reports 400 farmers had started a week of protests near Antwerp, but the relation between that campaign-level count and simultaneous attendance at this port blockade is not explicit. Keep eligibility pending_threshold.

start_date.summary: The report states the Zeebrugge blockade took place Tuesday 30 January 2024.

location.summary: The event is at the Port of Zeebrugge; all access roads were reported blocked.

demands.summary: Farmers objected to prices received/cheap imports and EU environmental rules; an ABS representative explicitly asked the Belgian and European governments for farmer-friendly policy and a correct price.

participants_original.summary: 400 farmers began a week of protests near Antwerp, but no exact simultaneous turnout at Zeebrugge is given.

organizer.summary: ABS called on members to join the protest; exact event organizer remains unclear.

state_response.summary: No specific response variable is established; the Prime Minister’s statement addressing concerns is not coded as accommodation.

notes: A source describes a wider wave of Belgian farmer protests underway for days and a week-long action near Antwerp; this candidate is the specific Zeebrugge port blockade and should not automatically absorb nearby Brussels or other local actions. EU institutions/policy are among the targets, but the source also explicitly quotes a demand addressed to the Belgian government; therefore it is not treated as EU-only. The report says farmers planned to continue to midnight Wednesday, which is not verified physical end.
open_questions: Does the 400-farmer figure describe this port gathering simultaneously or the wider week-long series?
Did this specific port blockade end as planned at midnight Wednesday, and did it continue beyond that point?
Were there distinct preceding or subsequent local actions, or one connected week-long episode?
What, if any, Belgian-government response followed the demand?

title: Tractor convoy arrives in Brussels ahead of the EU-summit farmers’ protest
location: Brussels-Capital Region; convoy passed through the city and headed toward the European Quarter
participants_original: The Brussels Times reports a first tractor convoy entered Brussels at about 18:30, another was still entering around 23:00, and about 60 tractors passed through Halle. It gives no person count for the Brussels convoy.
threshold_50_evidence: No person attendance count is given for the Jan31 Brussels convoy. The 60-tractor count refers to a convoy in Halle and is not converted into a protester count. Eligibility remains pending evidence.

start_date.summary: The report says the first convoy drove into the Brussels-Capital Region around 18:30 Wednesday 31 January.

location.summary: The convoy entered Brussels and moved toward the European Quarter; tractors were pictured at Place du Trône.

participants_original.summary: About 60 tractors were reported in Halle; the Brussels convoy has no person attendance count.

demands.summary: The article does not identify a specific demand for the Jan31 convoy; it says a larger protest was expected the next day alongside an EU summit.

notes: Keep the Jan31 convoy separate from the announced Feb1 gathering until occurrence, threshold, demand and episode continuity are established. The Feb1 event is an announcement in this article, not evidence of execution. The Jan30 Zeebrugge blockade is another local action; no merger is inferred.
open_questions: Did the Jan31 convoy itself express a demand aimed at Belgian government/policy, the EU institutions, or both?
How many people were physically present in the Brussels convoy and was it a public political gathering rather than merely transport to the next day’s protest?
Is the convoy a distinct episode from the Jan30 Zeebrugge blockade and Feb1 protest?
When did this convoy/action physically end?
